WHAT WAS BUILT — G1 tokens (wiring, NOT a re-implementation): collect_tokens(root, run_dir, date, results) reads per-lane token counts mechanically into lanes.json and tokens.json. Priority: (1) a `[runner] tokens_in=N tokens_out=M` line in each lane's trailer.log (per-lane, most precise, forward-compatible); (2) `tools/token-capture.py --json --cwd <root> --since <date>` — T521's instrument — joined on the canonical lane label via its `models` map. A lane with no reading is `null` + a `tokens_missing_reason`, never estimated, and the field is always present (never absent). write_tokens_summary() derives tokens.json from the same collection (no second source to drift).

COORDINATION WITH T521 (stated explicitly, not a silent gap): T521's token-capture.py is per-TASK, keyed on the dispatch prompt naming `untracked/T<id>` / `claim T<id>`; bakeoff lanes carry MANAGENT_TASK_ID=bakeoff/<run>/<label> (NOT a T-id), so the per-lane join here is on the model label via the `models` map, scoped by `--since <run date>`. Known limitation flagged to T521/Orchestrator: two same-model sessions the same day (a race lane + a non-race task) are confounded at day granularity; a lane-level session key would close it. The interface this row needs is therefore: token-capture.py exposing per-model tokens_in/tokens_out via `--json --cwd <root> --since <date>` (already true) OR a lane/session-keyed reading.

G2 isolation (refuse, don't record): assess_isolation(root) + enforce_g2() refuse to dispatch (exit 2, naming G2) unless root_is_worktree is true AND no key/rubric secret is reachable by relative path. --allow-unisolated '<reason>' overrides loudly and is recorded in lanes.json (isolation.allow_unisolated / allow_unisolated_reason). IMPORTANT NUANCE found while testing: untracked/race-grading/ is NOT absent from a fresh worktree — two grader OUTPUT files (t452/scores-glm-5.2.md, t452/scores-kimi-k2.7.md) are force-committed despite the untracked/ gitignore, so a bare os.path.exists(race-grading) check would false-refuse every legitimate worktree run. The check therefore tests for the SECRET markers only: untracked/race-keys (any existence) and, under race-grading, README.md / anonymize.py / race1 / t447 / t452/lanes-map.sealed.json / t452/KEY.md. The boundary remains honestly labelled a relative-path boundary, not a sandbox (T376).

G3 family exclusion (hard refusal at counting): model_family(label) derives claude/deepseek/glm/qwen/minimax/kimi from the canonical label — FINER than the roster's dispatch family (deepseek/claude/ollama), because glm/minimax/kimi/qwen are four different model families despite all being ollama-served (the grand-race §2 arithmetic — Claude lanes graded by the DS pair + qwen — rests on this). grade_family() annotates is_self/is_family and NEVER raises (retention is unconditional); count_grade() raises FamilyGradeError on a family grade, and count_grades() refuses rather than filters.

G4 blinding (sanitizer before grading): sanitize_out(out_path) writes out.sanitized.md alongside the original; the original is NEVER modified (it is evidence). Self-identifying text is detected via first-person/attribution constructions (I am Claude / as a DeepSeek model / I'm GLM), canonical model labels, and capitalized family proper nouns (lowercase 'minimax' the Go algorithm and lowercase 'glm' are deliberately NOT matched). A self-identifying lane is FLAGGED in lanes.json (self_identified, self_id_matches, sanitized_out) — the flag is itself a data point, not a silent scrub.
